_source: CLAUDE.md §38 BACKTEST INVALIDATION. The ten bullets below are §38's own list, in §38's own order and wording. scripts/tests/test_research_validity.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md, so an eleventh bullet in the spec fails the build rather than going undetected.
_reader: scripts/research_validity.py is the ONE reader. Nothing else may decide what a defect means to a run.
_rule: §38's sentence is 'flagged OR invalidated'. Which of the two a condition gets is declared here, once, with the reason -- not chosen per call site, where it would drift toward whichever verdict was convenient that day. A caller may ESCALATE a FLAGS condition to INVALIDATES when it has evidence the defect was worse than the general case. A caller may NEVER downgrade INVALIDATES; research_validity.Assessment.finding() raises.
_dispositions_test: The line between the two is the DIRECTION OF THE ERROR. INVALIDATES = the run's numbers are about trades that could not have been taken as measured, and the error runs in an unbounded, usually flattering direction (the future got in). FLAGS = the run measured something real, but not the thing it claims: a narrower dataset, a less-constrained system, a cheaper venue. A flagged result is evidence about a different system; an invalid result is not evidence.

dispositions.FLAGS: The run stays readable and its verdict becomes FLAGGED. The finding travels with every number it produced.
dispositions.INVALIDATES: The run's verdict becomes INVALID. Per §38 its performance figures may not be presented as a result, and consumers that SELECT on performance (scripts/rank-setups.py) must refuse it.

verdicts.VALID: Every declared condition was checked or declared not-applicable for this run, and none fired.
verdicts.FLAGGED: At least one FLAGS condition fired and no INVALIDATES condition did.
verdicts.INVALID: At least one INVALIDATES condition fired.
verdicts.UNVERIFIED: No condition fired, but at least one was never looked at. NOT one of §38's two words -- it is the honest third state that keeps 'nobody checked' from rendering as 'passed', which is the exact failure §38's last sentence names.

conditions.why: A decision that moved when the future moved was not a decision; it was a reading of the answer. §37: future movement may determine the OUTCOME and nothing else.
conditions.evidence: A probe report with violations. research_validity.from_leakage() turns each into a finding.

conditions.why: Same defect as look-ahead reached by a different road (a derived series computed over the whole history, a parameter fitted on the test window). The result is the same: the measured system could not have been run.
conditions._detector_why: scripts/leakage.py catches the consequence look-ahead and leakage SHARE -- a past decision that moves when the future moves -- and a probe violation is recorded under look_ahead, so this condition is the residual: the leakage a probe structurally cannot see. Mutating one series' future does not disturb a parameter that was already fitted over the whole history, a threshold chosen after looking at the results, or a symbol set assembled from survivors; those are baked in before the probe runs. §9's bias register already names the two live instances (data snooping: 7 ICT-target variants over one dataset, undisclosed; survivorship: the allowlist holds only currently-listed symbols). Owners: §43 experiment budget, §45 validation.

conditions.why: Time order IS the experiment. If a bar repeats a timestamp, goes backwards, or carries something that is not a timestamp, then 'the information available at the historical decision time' has no referent and no PIT claim about the run can be true or false.
conditions.detector: scripts/quality.py assess() -> INVALID whose reason names a timestamp fault (`_structural_fault`)
conditions.evidence: backtest-methods.QUALITY_FLAGS; research_validity.from_quality_flags() routes timestamp faults here and every other INVALID to corrupted_provider_data.

conditions.why: §28/§29: a calendar revision, a cancellation or a later classification change reaching an earlier decision is look-ahead wearing a news filter. It flatters in the same unbounded direction, because the revision is usually what actually happened.
conditions._detector_why: No backtest in this repo reads a calendar at all -- the configuration snapshot records `event_risk.calendar` under `declared_but_not_applied_by_this_engine`, which is the incomplete_required_inputs condition, not this one. This condition becomes checkable the moment a calendar joins a research run, and scripts/event_risk.py already refuses to load one without a snapshot id (§29). Declared now so that day cannot arrive without a verdict attached.

conditions.why: A hole narrows what the run measured; it does not let the future in. §20 is blunt that an indicator computed over a holey window 'is not a degraded one, it is a different one', so the result is evidence about a different series and must say so -- but the trades it did book were booked on real bars in real order.

An unmodelled cost or venue constraint makes the run a measurement of a cheaper, more permissive venue than the one that trades. That is a real measurement of a different system, and the direction of the error is known and statable -- which is what separates it from the look-ahead family.
conditions.evidence: The engine declares what it does and does not model in one dict; research_validity.from_execution_assumptions() raises one finding naming everything unmodelled. Standing, not incidental: every run of this engine carries it.

conditions.why: A candle whose high is below its low, or whose close sits outside its range, is a bad bar -- the rules read it and got nonsense. Nonsense is not a claim about the future, and one bad bar in forty thousand does not make the other forty thousand a lie, so §38's first word applies. Escalate when the corruption is widespread enough to be the result.
conditions.detector: scripts/quality.py assess() -> INVALID (structural faults other than timestamps)

conditions.why: A dependency the Trading System declares REQUIRED_FOR_DECISION (§35) that the engine never consults. The three this engine omits -- event_risk.calendar, account.profile_rules, venue.reconciliation -- are all GATES: omitting a gate can only ADD trades, so the run measures a superset of the live system, not a flattered version of it. That is why it flags rather than invalidates. THE TEST, and it is not a loophole: omitting a dependency INVALIDATES the moment it could change a trade's TERMS rather than only its existence -- an omitted sizing input, an omitted stop rule, an omitted price source. Escalate then.
conditions.evidence: research_validity.from_config_snapshot() reads the §11 configuration snapshot the run already takes.

conditions.why: Rules that did not exist at the historical decision time, applied to it. §47 calls a methodology/setup/entry change version-significant precisely because the old numbers stop describing the new rules; a run that mixes the two describes neither.
conditions._detector_why: scripts/setup_version.py stamps the rule version a SETUP carries (§14), which is the ingredient a detector needs, but nothing yet compares a stored research result's stamped version against the rules a re-run would apply. Until that comparison exists this condition is UNVERIFIED on every run rather than silently clear -- see the `UNVERIFIED` verdict above. Owner: §47.

conditions.why: §44: once an out-of-sample period has influenced candidate or parameter selection it is exposed, and a result that still presents it as pristine validation overstates its own evidence without bound.
conditions._detector_why: §44 (OOS exposure tracking) is not implemented -- there is no experiment history to ask, so exposure cannot be computed. §9's bias register already records the untracked selection pressure (120 candidate rows -> 6 setups, nothing recorded). Owner: §44.
